units.text: INT. FAN - CONTINUOUS
My dear fellow, what on earth should we men do going about with purity and innocence? A carefully thought-out buttonhole is much more effective.
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: She doesn’t really love you then?
units.name: DUMBY

units.text: No, she does not!
units.name: LORD DARLINGTON

units.text: I congratulate you, my dear fellow. In this world there are only two tragedies. One is not getting what one wants, and the other is getting it. The last is much the worst; the last is a real tragedy! But I am interested to hear she does not love you. How long could you love a woman who didn’t love you, Cecil?
units.name: DUMBY

units.text: A woman who didn’t love me? Oh, all my life!
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: So could I. But it’s so difficult to meet one.
units.name: DUMBY

units.text: How can you be so conceited, DUMBY?
units.name: LORD DARLINGTON

units.text: I didn’t say it as a matter of conceit. I said it as a matter of regret. I have been wildly, madly adored. I am sorry I have. It has been an immense nuisance. I should like to be allowed a little time to myself now and then.
units.name: DUMBY

units.text: Looking round .
Time to educate yourself, I suppose.
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: No, time to forget all I have learned. That is much more important, dear Tuppy.
units.name: DUMBY

units.text: LORD AUGUSTUS moves uneasily in his chair .
What cynics you fellows are!
units.name: LORD DARLINGTON

units.text: What is a cynic?
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: Sitting on the back of the sofa .
A man who knows the price of everything and the value of nothing.
units.name: LORD DARLINGTON

units.text: And a sentimentalist, my dear Darlington, is a man who sees an absurd value in everything, and doesn’t know the market price of any single thing.
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: You always amuse me, Cecil. You talk as if you were a man of experience.
units.name: LORD DARLINGTON

units.text: I am.
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: Moves up to front off fireplace .
You are far too young!
units.name: LORD DARLINGTON

units.text: That is a great error. Experience is a question of instinct about life. I have got it. Tuppy hasn’t. Experience is the name Tuppy gives to his mistakes. That is all.
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: LORD AUGUSTUS looks round indignantly .
Experience is the name every one gives to their mistakes.
units.name: DUMBY

units.text: Standing with his back to the fireplace .
One shouldn’t commit any.
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: Sees LADY WINDERMERE’S fan on sofa .
Life would be very dull without them.
units.name: DUMBY

units.text: Of course you are quite faithful to this woman you are in love with, Darlington, to this good woman?
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: Cecil, if one really loves a woman, all other women in the world become absolutely meaningless to one. Love changes one— I am changed.
units.name: LORD DARLINGTON

units.text: Dear me! How very interesting! Tuppy, I want to talk to you.
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: LORD AUGUSTUS takes no notice .
It’s no use talking to Tuppy. You might just as well talk to a brick wall.
units.name: DUMBY

units.text: But I like talking to a brick wall—it’s the only thing in the world that never contradicts me! Tuppy!
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: Well, what is it? What is it?
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: Rising and going over to CECIL GRAHAM.
Come over here. I want you particularly.
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: Aside .
Darlington has been moralising and talking about the purity of love, and that sort of thing, and he has got some woman in his rooms all the time.
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: No, really! really!
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: In a low voice .
Yes, here is her fan.
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: Points to the fan .
Chuckling .
By Jove! By Jove!
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS
